notes: Chunk 47 covers six Common Crawl captures groups (11 text files, all readable) for Berkeley-Haas and UCLA Anderson. sourceUrl is the Common Crawl index lookup address from each file footer; sourceDate is the capture timestamp date. Points for the integrator: (1) Haas job-market pages: all three snapshots (two 2015 captures of the same page at two paths, one Oct 2016 capture) say "candidates on the job market in 2015-16"; recorded as listedYear 2016 / job-market with the range in note. The Oct 2016 capture may be a stale page that still carries the 2015-16 heading while listing added names (Jenny Zha Giedt, Parham Holakouee, Yujin Kim, Angus Hildreth), so its season could really be 2016-17; it also lists Scott Roeder under both Marketing and Operations Management (one record, program "Marketing; Operations Management"). (2) Haas Management of Organizations "Dissertations & Placements": entries read "Name, YYYY" then placement then dissertation; the page never says whether the year is graduation or placement, so yearMeaning is "unstated". The sidebar profile "Christopher Rider PhD 08" matches "Christopher I. Rider, 2008", which suggests degree year, but this is not stated. Some destinations are non-academic (Google, Inc.; Goldman Sachs & Co.) or visiting/fellow roles (NYU Stern Visiting Scholar; Harvard Research Fellow). (3) Haas Alumni Network page: nine profiles with the year given only as "PhD 10" style labels (recorded as graduation, 2000+NN, with the label quoted in note); destination/position are the profile's current affiliation at capture time, not a stated first job; program is not stated on the page. (4) UCLA Anderson "Dissertations" page: an alphabetical list of 896 (2015) / 962 (2016) dissertation entries "SURNAME, Given: Title" with no years, no programs and no placements. In the capture several entries run together on one line (25 lines in 2015, 4 in 2016, e.g. "COFF, Russel: ... COGET, Jean-Francois A.H.: ..."); these were split programmatically at the next "SURNAME, Given: " start and each split was reviewed by eye. One 2016 entry is written "ASSUNCAO: Joao Luis: The Rational Relationship..." (colon instead of comma); it is recorded as "ASSUNCAO, Joao Luis" with the written form quoted in note. Otherwise names are kept exactly as written (surname in capitals; a few entries have no given name, e.g. "ABOU-AISH", and 2016 writes "Mac CRIMMON" / "Mac KENZIE" where 2015 wrote "MacCRIMMON" / "MacKENZIE"). People listed more than once (multi-volume dissertations, or two titles under one name such as "McALLISTER, Donald Michael") get a single record per snapshot with all titles in note. The page covers the whole doctoral history of the school, including pre-1999 graduates, with no degree-year evidence. (5) UCLA Anderson "Placement" page: "Recent Academic Placement of our Ph.D. Graduates ... completed their Ph.D. in 1999 or later and who accepted faculty positions"; each entry gives "Year of Graduation", "First academic placement", dissertation title and chair(s); several entries run together on one line and were split programmatically (next name taken as the text after the single-surname chair names). Destinations are copied as written, including "No placement" (Aparupa Das Gupta 2014, Mirei Takashima 2016, Bo Kyung Kim 2013), industry/post-doc entries (Brattle Group, Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Federal Reserve Board/Bank, World Bank, "Post Doc - UCLA Economics Department", "Post Doc- Carnegie Mellon", "Post Doc-University of Michigan") and label typos ("Firs academic placement", "First academic plancement"). Program headings are the page's own ("Decisions, Operations, and Technology Management", "International Business and Comparative Management", "Information Systems"). The 2016 capture adds 2014-2016 graduates and corrects a few earlier entries (e.g. Tatsuo Ushijima's chair, Hong Kong UST spelling, Yihong Xia's placement wording); both snapshots are kept separately. The sidebar "Ph.D. Students" surname lists (current students) and the "2015-16/2016-17 Job Market Candidates" nav link carry no graduate names and were skipped.
